If A is a 2×2 matrix A with characteristic polynomial p(x)=x2+3x−2, then A4=

b
−39A+22I
c
−12A+53I

−21A+2I
e

Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, let's divide the polynomial f(x)=x4 by characteristic polynomial p(x)=x2+3x−2, using long division:

x2 − 3x + 11
x2+3x−2 x4|
x4 + 3x3 − 2x2
− 3x3 + 2x2
− 3x3 − 9x2 + 6x
11x2 − 6x
11x2 + 33x − 22
− 39x + 22

Therefore, we can write x4 as

x4=q(x)p(x)+(−39x+22), where q(x)=x2−3x+11. Replacing x with A, we have

A4=q(A)p(A)+(−39A+22I).

Now, according to the Cayley-Hamilton theorem, we have p(A)=O. Therefore,

A4=q(A)p(A)+(−39A+22I)=q(A)⋅O+(−39A+22I)=−39A+22I.
